newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia crop yields likely below average-ABARE.
newsitem.headline: Australia crop yields likely below average-ABARE.

text.p: Prospects of drier than normal seasonal conditions in Australia due to an emerging El Nino weather phenomenon mean that crop yields are likely to be below average, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Wednesday.
However, it was not possible to be precise about the areas of australia that will be most affected by El Nino, ABARE said in its latest crop report.

Depending on future rains, it is still possible to achieve above-average yields, ABARE said, noting that in two recent years affected by El Nino in June, wheat yields were 35 percent below average in one and just above average in the other.
ABARE said it has maintained its earlier estimate of Australian wheat production of 16.3 million tonnes and total winter crop plantings of just over 18 million hectares in 1997/98.
"Despite the very dry conditions across eastern Australia in March and April, rainfall received in May and June has been sufficient for planting expectations to be met in many areas," ABARE said.
